description:
Advances: ancora.derive

SECURITY. Filed 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator of ancora-xla, from a finding by the ancora-xla.8 cold verifier, settled by its auditor, and reproduced independently a third time before filing. Priority P0 for triage, not because exploitation is easy, but because ancora is a gate that runs against repositories its operator does not control.

WHAT HAPPENS

Ancora.BaseView.materialize writes every blob from a git tree listing into a temp root, using the path git reports verbatim. A git tree may contain an entry literally named "..". When it does, git ls-tree -r emits a path containing that component, git resolves it on read, and Path.join leaves it in place, so the kernel resolves it at File.write! and the file lands OUTSIDE the temp root. Depth is attacker-chosen: more nested ".." entries move the write further up. The escaped file also survives the File.rm_rf(base_root) cleanup at lib/ancora/gate.ex:67 and lib/ancora/review.ex:41, because it was never inside base_root to begin with.

Nothing between ls_tree_entries and the write validates the path. The read string and the write string are the same verbatim ls-tree path.

REPRODUCTION, confirmed on git 2.49.0, run three times by three different agents

Build the tree with plumbing. Nest a directory entry "a", then an entry named "..", then another entry named "..", holding the blob:

  B=$(git rev-parse HEAD:f.txt)
  L3=$(printf '100644 blob %s\tevil.txt\n' "$B" | git mktree)
  L2=$(printf '040000 tree %s\t..\n' "$L3" | git mktree)
  L1=$(printf '040000 tree %s\t..\n' "$L2" | git mktree)
  TOP=$(printf '040000 tree %s\ta\n' "$L1" | git mktree)
  C=$(git commit-tree "$TOP" -m hostile)

Observed:
- git mktree ACCEPTS an entry named ".." without complaint.
- git ls-tree -r emits: 100644 blob <sha>\ta/../../evil.txt
- printf '%s\n' "$C:a/../../evil.txt" | git cat-file --batch returns the blob header and payload, exit 0.
- Path.expand(Path.join("/tmp/ancora-base-ROOT/sub", "a/../../evil.txt")) is /tmp/ancora-base-ROOT/evil.txt, one directory above the join root.
- The auditor ran the real production functions: Ancora.BaseView.blobs returned the escaped path mapped to its content, and materialize wrote the payload one directory above its own root under a pinned TMPDIR. With five ".." levels it landed five directories up.

WHY IT WAS INITIALLY MISSED, worth recording because it will mislead the next reader too

Git normalizes a <rev>:<path> string ONLY when the path begins with "./" or "../". That is the code path producing "fatal: ... is outside repository". Any other string is walked literally, component by component, against tree entry NAMES, so an embedded ".." matches an entry literally named "..". Confirmed from both sides:
- "<rev>:../evil.txt" is REFUSED as outside repository.
- "<rev>:a/./../../evil.txt" fails with path-does-not-exist, because no entry is named ".".
- "<rev>:a/../../evil.txt" SUCCEEDS.

So a two-level probe finds nothing and looks conclusive. My own first reproduction stopped there and wrongly concluded the escape was unreachable. Three levels is the shape that works.

BOTH READ PATHS ARE AFFECTED. The auditor confirmed blobs through a live RunContext with the batch port open returns byte-identical hostile content, so this is not limited to the no-port fallback.

RECOMMENDED FIX, and it is small

Reject any tree entry whose path contains a ".." component, inside read_tree_blobs, before the read and before the write. No new module, no process, no registry: this epic's governing principle is that ancora carries less machinery than the project it was split from, and this needs none. A rejected entry should produce a finding rather than a crash, consistent with ancora-xla.2's environment-tier work, and the whole tree should probably be refused rather than the single entry skipped, since a repository containing such an entry is hostile rather than unlucky.

Add a test that builds the hostile tree with plumbing exactly as above and asserts nothing is written outside the root. A test asserting only that the read is refused would not catch a future change that reintroduces the write.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED IN ancora-xla.8

That ticket permits lib/ancora/base_view.ex for a COMMENT ONLY, and its Out of Scope forbids changing materialize behaviour, on the stated premise that this defence already held. That premise is what turned out to be false. ancora-xla.8 is being bounced to correct only its comment, which currently asserts that git rejects these entries.

Manuel: this is a real finding and it is yours to prioritise. Nothing in the epic depends on it, and it is filed standalone rather than adopted, so it does not block anything.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTRACT (appended by /investigate 2026-09-04; original above is untouched)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Ready-for: implement

Deliverable:
Reject any git tree whose ls-tree path contains an unsafe component, before any
base blob is read or written, so a hostile repository cannot escape the
materialization root. Concretely, in Ancora.BaseView.read_tree_blobs/2
(lib/ancora/base_view.ex:77-93): split each entry's byte-exact path on "/" and,
if any component is exactly "..", ".", or "" (empty), refuse the WHOLE tree by
halting the reduce with {:env, message}, before Git.read_blob and before
materialize/3 creates its temp root. Widen the @spec of blobs/3 and
materialize/3 to include {:env, String.t()}. Remove the now-stale honest comment
at base_view.ex:82-83 that says the escape is unfixed and tracked as ancora-kzw.

The check must be component-wise, not a substring test: "foo..bar" is a single
legitimate component and must pass. ".." is the traversal vector; "." and empty
mark a malformed tree a trusted repo never produces and cost nothing to reject.

Error surfacing (both callers must reach the env tier, neither may raise):
- gate.ex run/3 else (around lib/ancora/gate.ex:116) currently has only
  {:error, reason} -> gate_error(reason). Add {:env, _} = error -> error so the
  {:env, message} from materialize propagates as Gate.check/2's existing
  {:env, String.t()} result. Without this line, {:env, _} matches no else clause
  and raises WithClauseError.
- review.ex build_with_context (lib/ancora/review.ex:44-57) already forwards
  {:env, _} and needs NO change under this design. Do not switch to an
  {:error, tuple} shape, which would require a new review.ex else clause and, if
  omitted, reproduces the "review assembly failed" no-verdict crash.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/base_view_test.exs (new hostile-tree test),
  test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/ancora/review_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate:
  1. A tree built with plumbing (git hash-object -w, git mktree an inner tree
     with an entry named "..", nested under an outer "a" tree so ls-tree -r
     yields "a/../../evil.txt") causes materialize to return {:env, message};
     the temp root is never created; and the escape target does NOT exist
     anywhere outside the root. Assert the FILESYSTEM property (nothing written
     outside the root), not merely that a read was refused. A read-only
     assertion would miss a future change that reintroduces the write.
  2. A legitimate path containing "foo..bar" as a component still materializes.
  3. Ancora.Review.build against the hostile repo returns {:env, _}, not a
     raise, so the two callers cannot silently diverge.
- Security measurement that proves the ticket's claim (read after the fix):
  run the probe in the investigation report against the fixed tree.
  BEFORE: BaseView.materialize(hostile_repo, hostile_commit, temp_root: pinned)
  returns {:ok, _} and writes evil.txt one directory ABOVE the pinned root.
  AFTER: the same call returns {:env, _} and no file exists outside the root.
  This is the number the fix must hit: files written outside base_root == 0 for
  a tree carrying any ".." component, at any nesting depth.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration: mix test on the named files, plus mix spec.validate. No full
    suite mid-iteration.
  - Final (run-until-green before IMPLEMENTED): mix compile --warnings-as-errors
    && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock
    --check-unused && mix spec.check --base origin/beadwork
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base origin/beadwork plus the tagged and
    --stale selections only.

Test isolation (bounce-class):
- Pin materialize's :temp_root under a fresh per-test parent directory and
  compute the escape target inside that parent, so a regression writes into the
  sandbox, never the working tree or CI home. on_exit rm_rf the parent, and
  best-effort delete the escape target, so a failing run cannot poison a rerun.
- One TmpGitRepo per test; async only where the fixture allows.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/git.ex (this is NOT a Git-layer change; the check belongs in
  BaseView, the only write-to-disk caller; change-set prefetch reads by OID and
  never writes a tree path to disk)
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- .spec/config.yml
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex and the change-set prefetch path

Allowed touches:
- lib/ancora/base_view.ex (the guard, the @spec widen, remove the stale comment)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (the one {:env, _} else line only)
- test/ancora/base_view_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs,
  test/ancora/review_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (requirement ancora.derive.base_reads_batched
  and/or scenario ancora.derive.scenario.narrowed_base_materialization:
  substantive statement that BaseView rejects a tree whose entry path carries a
  "..", ".", or empty component before any read or write. This is the edit that
  clears derived/drift on base_view.ex; a Spec-Ack trailer is NOT acceptable
  here because the contract genuinely changes.)
- .spec/decisions/** (editing any .spec/specs/ path fires change/missing_decision
  via Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 unless a decision record changes in
  the same diff. Amend ancora.decision.field_friction_response.md, which already
  affects ancora.derive, with a real statement recording the hostile-tree
  rejection rule, OR add one focused decision. Do NOT add a hollow line to
  silence the finding; a grader will bounce it.)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No change to how well-formed trees materialize.
- No new module, process, registry, or finding code. The finding registry is
  closed; hostile trees surface through the existing {:env, message} tier.
- Do not fix the separate latent {:error, {:temp_directory, _}} raise in
  review.ex; it is a different defect and out of scope here.

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base origin/beadwork ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs
- [ ] The security measurement above shows 0 files written outside base_root for
      a ".." tree at multiple nesting depths

Decision:
Guard in Ancora.BaseView.read_tree_blobs/2 (not Ancora.Git, not materialize's
write loop), reject the whole tree on any "..", ".", or empty path component
(component-split, never substring), and return {:env, message}. BaseView is the
only caller that writes tree paths to disk, so a Git-layer guard would refuse
harmless ".." trees on the read-only change-set path; write-time guarding is too
late because the temp root already exists. The {:env, message} return is chosen
over {:error, {:unsafe_tree_path, _}} on a measured fact: gate.ex routes
materialize errors through gate_error while review.ex RAISES on {:error, _} and
only forwards {:env, _}; the env return reaches the env tier through both callers
with one edit (a gate.ex else line), whereas the error-tuple shape needs three
edits and reintroduces the no-verdict crash if the review.ex clause is forgotten.
Rejected: Git-layer guard (over-broad, killed by the change-set-reads-by-OID
fact); write-time guard (temp root already made); skip-the-entry (silent partial
base view yields a wrong drift verdict); substring "..\" match (rejects
foo..bar); a new finding code (registry is closed).

Open Questions:
None.
